newsitem.title: UK: International LPG weak in Europe, steady in Asia.
newsitem.headline: International LPG weak in Europe, steady in Asia.

text.p: European liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices weakened in line with naphtha and crude this week, traders and brokers said.
East Asian prices remained stable as buyers awaited the publication of new posted prices for July.
Propane in the North Sea market was discussed in a wide range.

The only serious buyers were either petrochemical buyers or traders covering short positions into petrochemical buyers, a trader said. But bids reflected the point at which propane becomes competitive with alternative feedstock naphtha.
This is reached when propane is valued in the mid $170's a tonne, a dealer said.
By contrast offers came from the mid $180's a tonne. At least one seller said he believed the next deal will be done at over $180 a tonne.
"I don't think we'll see propane deals below $180 as traders will still have to cover," he said. But discussion was thin, and no significant large cargo deals were recorded.
A 5,000 tonne butane cargo was traded at $180 a tonne cif Antwerp for early July delivery on Thursday, with a petrochemical company buying the piece for cracking.
But little other interest was heard for butane, and a dealer said that both propane and butane were valued at approximately the same level.
"The arbs are not really working," said a trader in the North Sea market, adding that there was little arbitrage opportunity for moving material either into or out of the northwest European market.
While North Sea prices remained high, there was an incentive for sellers to offer Algerian material into northwest Europe as well as into the US Gulf Coast and the local Mediterranean market.
But lower prices have limited such opportunities, and the north west European market has become self-contained, he added.
Premiums over the Saudi Contract Price (CP), the main benchmark for LPG in the Asian markets, have been stable over the week.

"Spot buyers are still on the sidelines," a dealer said, "and nominal levels are unchanged." The CP for July will be published at the end of the month, and traders are not expecting any great interest in trade until that appears.
Japanese buyers traditionally fill their inventories in the summer, when prices are at their lowest, ahead of the peak winter demand period.
This year, a trader said, there is a belief that the current CP is near the bottom. If the July CP is higher, people will believe the market has moved irrevocably into contango.
And if this happens, the trader said, there will probably be a rush of purchases in July ahead of a feared new increase in August.
But until the new price is published, no real activity is expected.
"The key factor is the coming CP," the trader said. In the absence of current deals, Japanese prices are assessed by adding freight to spot fob levels in the Middle East Gulf.

Levels there are steady at around CP -$3 a tonne for propane and around CP flat for butane, with freight to Japan assessed at around $30 a tonne. As a result, buyers are bidding approximately CP + $26 a tonne for propane, with offers coming from around CP + $33 a tonne.
--Sebastian Alison, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 6412
